posts.headline: Under the WARN Act, how much notice is due before a plant closing?
posts.explain: Covered employers (generally 100+ employees) must give 60 calendar days' written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff.
posts.sourceLine: Source: 29 U.S.C. § 2102(a); 20 CFR Part 639; U.S. DOL

posts.facebook_first_comment:
✅ Answer: C. 60 days.
Federal WARN covers employers with 100+ employees and requires 60 calendar days' written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff. Some states go further with their own "mini-WARN" laws (New York and New Jersey require 90 days), but the federal answer is 60.

posts.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under the federal WARN Act, how much advance written notice must a covered employer give before a plant closing?
A. 30 days
B. 45 days
C. 60 days
D. 90 days
posts.alt_a: Answer: C. 60 days. Covered employers (generally 100+ employees) must give 60 calendar days' written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff.

youtube_quiz.question: Under the federal WARN Act, how much advance written notice must a covered employer give before a plant closing?
youtube_quiz.explanation: Federal WARN requires 60 calendar days' written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff (employers with 100+ employees). Some state mini-WARN laws require 90.

sources: U.S. DOL: Plant Closings and Layoffs

posts.facebook_first_comment:
✅ Answer: C. 5 years.
Under USERRA, cumulative service with one employer can total up to 5 years and the employee keeps reemployment rights. Some service doesn't count toward the 5 years, like required annual training and certain involuntary call-ups. 🇺🇸 Thank you to every veteran today.
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com
posts.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under USERRA, an employee generally keeps reemployment rights with one employer for up to how much cumulative military service?
A. 1 year
B. 2 years
C. 5 years
D. No limit
posts.alt_a: Answer: C. 5 years. Service with one employer can total up to 5 years. Some service, like annual training and certain call-ups, doesn't count toward the cap.

youtube_quiz.question: Under USERRA, an employee generally keeps reemployment rights with one employer for up to how much cumulative military service?
youtube_quiz.explanation: USERRA's cumulative limit is 5 years of service with one employer. Certain service (e.g. annual training, some involuntary call-ups) is exempt from the cap.

sources: U.S. DOL VETS: USERRA Pocket Guide

posts.label: EXAM TIP
posts.headline: Read the last line first.
posts.body: On long scenario questions, check what's being asked before you read the story: the FIRST step? The BEST response? Then you'll know which details matter.
posts.caption_instagram:
💡 SHRM-CP & SCP exam tip

Long scenario? Skip to the last line first. "What should HR do FIRST" and "What's the BEST response" are different questions, and knowing which one you're answering tells you what to look for in the story. 🔍

🔖 Save this for exam day.

held.facebook_first_comment:
✅ Answer: C. April 30.
The OSHA 300A summary of last year's work-related injuries and illnesses must be posted from February 1 to April 30, even if there were no recordable cases. (Employers with 10 or fewer employees and some low-hazard industries are generally exempt from keeping these records.)
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com
held.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Employers must post the OSHA Form 300A injury and illness summary starting February 1. Until when must it stay posted?
A. March 1
B. March 31
C. April 30
D. December 31
held.alt_a: Answer: C. April 30. Post last year's summary from February 1 to April 30 where employee notices usually go, even if there were zero cases.

youtube_quiz.question: Employers must post the OSHA Form 300A injury and illness summary starting February 1. Until when must it stay posted?
youtube_quiz.explanation: OSHA requires the Form 300A summary to be posted from February 1 to April 30, even with zero recordable cases.
